title: The First Game Boy Zelda Started as an After-Hours Side Project
hook:
Link's Awakening, the first handheld Zelda, began in the early nineties as one Nintendo programmer's after-hours experiment with no official project behind it. Which handheld Zelda is your favorite?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the first handheld Zelda game started as an after hours side project that nobody asked for? In the early nineties, Nintendo programmer Kazuaki Morita got hold of a Game Boy development kit. He began tinkering with it in his spare time to see if a Zelda game could run on the little gray handheld. Other members of the A Link to the Past team joined in after work. The team later compared it to an after school club. There was no official project at first. Once it looked promising, they took it to the company and got permission to keep going. The early idea was simply a Game Boy version of A Link to the Past. Director Takashi Tezuka wanted a world inspired by the TV show Twin Peaks, full of odd characters in one small place. The team also slipped in cameos from Goombas, Chain Chomps and even Kirby. Tezuka admitted he was not sure they ever got proper permission for those. The game became Link's Awakening, released on the Game Boy in June of nineteen ninety three. It later got a color version on the Game Boy Color, and years after that a full remake on the Switch. Not bad for a club activity. Which handheld Zelda is your favorite? Follow for more gaming history.
